He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]] and the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Ware grew up in [[North Little Rock, Arkansas]] and attended [[North Little Rock High School]].{{cite web |last=Davenport |first=Richard |date=May 7, 2021 |title=THE RECRUITING GUY: Ware keeps motor running on high |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/may/07/ware-keeps-motor-running-on-high/ |access-date=November 9, 2022 |work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]}} As a junior, he averaged 16.2 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 4.1 blocks per game. As a senior, Ware averaged 20.3 points, 12 rebounds, and 5.7 blocks per game.{{cite web |last=Davenport |first=Richard |date=January 26, 2022 |title=UA signees, Ware get all-star invite |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/jan/26/ua-signees-ware-get-all-star-invite/ |access-date=November 10, 2022 |work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]}} He also played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], [[Nike Hoop Summit]], and the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/highschoolsports/2022/04/future-oregon-duck-kelel-ware-to-play-in-nike-hoop-summit.html|title=Future Oregon Duck Kel’el Ware to play in Nike Hoop Summit|first=Nik|last=Streng|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Erick |date=March 29, 2022 |title=Arkansas connections galore at McDonald's game |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/mar/29/arkansas-connections-galore-at-mcdonalds-game/ |access-date=November 10, 2022 |work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/basketball/oregon-basketball-signee-kelel-ware-named-finalist-for-usa-basketball-u18-national-team|title=Oregon Signee Kel'el Ware Named Finalist for USA Basketball U18 National Team|first=Graham|last=Metzker|website=[[SI.com]]|date=June 2, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}} ===Recruiting=== Ware was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2022/01/updated-rankings-kelel-ware-oregon-ducks-center-signee-becomes-consensus-5-star-basketball-prospect.html|title=Updated rankings: Kel’el Ware, Oregon Ducks center signee, becomes consensus 5-star basketball prospect|first=Andrew|last=Nemec|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=January 19, 2022|access-date=November 9, 2022}} On August 9, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] over offers from [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web |last=Hansen |first=Chris |date=August 9, 2021 |title=Oregon Ducks land another 5-star recruit as 7–0 center Kel'el Ware commits |url=https://www.registerguard.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/08/09/oregon-ducks-land-another-5-star-recruit-7-0-center-kelel-ware-commits/5541311001 |access-date=November 9, 2022 |work=[[The Register Guard]]}} Ware was also offered a two-year contract for $900,000 from [[Overtime Elite]], but he declined offer and maintained his commitment to Oregon.{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2021/09/kelel-ware-oregon-ducks-5-star-center-pledge-declines-900000-offer-from-overtime-elite-remains-committed-report.html|title=Kel’el = 8 | accessdate = November 11, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Ware entered his freshman season at Oregon as the Ducks' second center.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon/Article/Oregon-Ducks-basketball-Kelel-Ware-Keeshawn-Barthelemy-197216052/|title=Dana Altman sees talent but also lots of room for improvement in newcomers Kel'el Ware, Keeshawn Barthelemy|first=Matt|last=Prehm|website=[[247Sports]]|date=November 9, 2022|access-date=November 9, 2022}} He also entered the season as a potential first-round selection in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/insider/story/_/id/34918359|title=Newcomer Impact Rankings: Which men's college basketball freshmen, transfers will lead teams in 2022–23?|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}} After averaging 26 minutes played, 10.3 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks over the first nine games of the season, Ware saw a decline in playing time due to what Oregon's coaching staff believed to be an inconsistent work ethic.{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2023/03/oregon-mens-basketball-center-kelel-ware-to-enter-transfer-portal.html|title=Oregon men’s basketball center Kel’el Ware to enter transfer portal|first=James|last=Crepea|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=March 27, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} He ultimately averaged 6.6 points and 4.1 rebounds per game on the season. At the end of the season, Ware entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35970015|title=Oregon's Kel'el Ware, former top-10 recruit, to enter portal|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 27, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} Ware ultimately transferred to [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/36151417|title=Oregon center Kel'el Ware transferring to Indiana|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=April 10, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} He started at center in the Hoosiers' season-opener against [[2023–24 Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball team|Florida Gulf Coast]] and recorded the first double-double of his college career with 13 points, 12 rebounds, four assists, three blocks, and two steals as Indiana won 69–63.{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2023/11/07/indiana-basketball-beats-fgcu-score-kelel-ware-gabe-cupps-debuts-iu-hoosiers-florida-gulf-coast/71473465007/|title=Indiana basketball beats FGCU thanks to Kel'el Ware, Gabe Cupps debuts|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=November 7, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} Ware set a new career-high with 22 points scored while also grabbing 12 rebounds on November 16, 2023, in a 89–80 victory over [[2023–24 Wright State Raiders men's basketball team|Wright State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2023/11/17/indiana-hoosiers-basketball-kelel-ware-playing-with-point-to-prove-iu-mike-woodson-oregon-transfer/71550763007/|title=Kel'el Ware came to IU with point to prove. He's playing like it, and Hoosiers need it.|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=November 17, 2023|access-date=November 17, 2023}} He re-set his career-high in scoring with 28 points in a 89–76 win over [[2023–24 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team|Harvard]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401577615|title=Career games for Ware and Mgbako lead Indiana past Harvard 89-76|work=[[ESPN]]|date=November 26, 2023|access-date=November 27, 2023}} After the season, Ware declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2024/03/26/indiana-basketball-kelel-ware-declares-for-2024-nba-draft-iu-hoosiers/72930443007/|title=Indiana basketball sophomore Kel'el Ware declares for 2024 NBA draft|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=March 26, 2024|access-date=March 26, 2024}} ==National team career== Ware played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/06/oregon-signee-kelel-ware-to-play-for-usa-basketballs-u18-mens-national-team.html|title=Oregon signee Kel’el Ware to play for USA Basketball’s U18 men’s national team|first=James|last=Crepea|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=June 3, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}} He was named to the All-Tournament team after averaging 15.7 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks as the United States won the gold medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/06/oregon-signee-kelel-ware-usa-basketballs-u18-mens-national-team-win-gold-at-americas-championship.html|title=Oregon signee Kel’el Ware, USA
